1. Open the Modules screen in the default theme.
1. Click the label "Start automatically" of the second row.

The checkbox of the first row is checked, and the checkbox of the second row stays unchecked.

<label for="moduleAutoStartVersion"> ... <input type="checkbox" name="moduleAutoStart" id="moduleAutoStartVersion" />
```

With two updates, the page holds two elements with `id="moduleAutoStartVersion"` and two labels that point at that id. A browser resolves `for` to the first element.

The label of each row toggles the checkbox of its own row. Each row needs an id of its own, such as one suffixed with the module id.

**Status:** open, test data (not a product defect)
**Spec:** `cypress/e2e/api-tests/009_policies/VM033.cy.js` — the four tests from `Create validation report` to `Approve verification report` are skipped (`it.skip`) with a pointer to this note.
**Fixtures:** `cypress/fixtures/valrep.json`, `cypress/fixtures/verrep.json` (last changed in 3.4.0-rc, `ac3de6e6c8`)

## What was observed

`VM033` passes up to `Verify report` (13 tests), then `Create validation report` answers 422:

```
POST /policies/{id}/tag/add_new_validation_report/blocks -> 422
JSON_SCHEMA_VALIDATION_ERROR ... must have required property 'projectTitle'
```

The spec never got this far before (it stopped at publish, then at `Create application`), so the fixtures were never checked against the current policy.

## Why

The two fixtures were written for an older version of the VM0033 schemas:

- `VVB Validation Report` (`#f4722f99-…` in `VM0033_7_23.policy`) requires `projectTitle`, `accountId` and `field0`. The fixture has `field0` and `field1`, but the schema has no `field1`. The report content now goes in `vcs_validation_report` (when `field0` is `VCS v4.4`) or `ccb_vcs_validation_report`. Those sub-schemas require fields the fixture does not have (`G206`, `G227`, `G231`, …), and the fixture has keys they do not define (`G103`, `G104`, …).
- `VVB Verification Report` has the same shape. Its `vcs_verification_report` sub-schema requires `monitoringReportId`, `monitoringReportName` and `reportName`, which the fixture does not have.

## How to reproduce

Run `VM033.cy.js` with its tag (it is not tagged `all`, so `npm run guardian:test` filters it out): `CYPRESS_grepTags=VM0033` with the environment of `scripts/local-guardian.sh test`. Then un-skip `Create validation report`.

## What a fix needs

Two report documents that are valid for the current schemas, with `projectTitle` and `accountId` taken from the project the report references. They can come from a regenerated fixture, or from the schema at run time (the UI's "Dry run with test data" uses `DocumentGenerator` from `@guardian/interfaces`). Then un-skip the four tests, run the spec twice, and delete this note.
title: bug (VM033): the validation and verification report fixtures do not match the VM0033 schemas

## Context

The jcontent Cypress suite still runs scenarios through the legacy page composer (GWT edit mode). The page composer has its own module and its own test suite in [Jahia/jahia-page-composer](https://github.com/Jahia/jahia-page-composer), so a test whose subject is the page composer belongs there. This issue moves those tests, and stops the jcontent tests that only used the page composer as a way to open Content Editor from depending on it.

## Tests to migrate to jahia-page-composer

These tests exercise the page composer itself, so they move to `tests/cypress/e2e/` of Jahia/jahia-page-composer and are removed from jcontent.

- [ ] `tests/cypress/e2e/contentEditor/shard1/previewContent.cy.ts`, the `via PageComposer` block (3 tests): the Content Editor preview of an edited page that is not the page currently rendered in the page composer, `template:include` rendering, and a parent node name with special characters.
- [ ] `tests/cypress/e2e/menuActions/deleteAdvanced.cy.ts`, the `Legacy Page Composer GWT Tests` block (1 test): the jContent delete, undelete and delete-permanently dialogs opened from the page composer context menu.
- [ ] `tests/cypress/e2e/contentEditor/shard2/editorUrl.cy.ts`, the test `Handles breadcrumb in GWT correctly`: a Content Editor URL hash opened in the page composer, and its breadcrumb navigating back to jContent.
- [ ] `tests/cypress/e2e/selectorTypes/systemNameTest.cy.ts`, the whole spec (7 tests): page creation through the page composer with an invalid name, Chinese characters, a reserved word, accented characters, special characters and `..`, the system name sync, and the 128-character limit. It overlaps `pageCreationTest.cy.ts` of jahia-page-composer (`Special characters are not allowed in system name`), so merge it there instead of adding a second spec.

The page objects of jahia-page-composer need what these tests call and do not have yet:

- `openDeleteDialog()`, `openUndeleteDialog()` and `openDeletePermanentlyDialog()` on the contextual menu.
- `checkSystemNameSync()` on `PageComposer`.
- jcontent's `createPage(title, save)` takes a positional boolean, while jahia-page-composer's takes `createPage(title, {systemName, save, template, under})`, so the calls of `systemNameTest` need adapting.
- `systemNameTest` enables `qa-module` on its site, which the jahia-page-composer provisioning does not install. Check whether the tests need it.

## Tests that stay in jcontent but stop using the page composer

These test Content Editor behaviour and only use the page composer to open the editor. Rewrite them to open Content Editor from jContent, so jcontent keeps the coverage.

- [ ] `tests/cypress/e2e/selectorTypes/textRegexInDefinition.cy.ts`: RegExp validation patterns. It needs `cent:testRegExp` from `jcontent-test-module`, which only the jcontent suite deploys.
- [ ] `tests/cypress/e2e/selectorTypes/addMixinChoicelistInitializers.cy.ts`: choice list initializers on `jnt:imageReferenceLink`. The spec is skipped today (`describe.skip`).
- [ ] `tests/cypress/e2e/selectorTypes/textFieldInitializerTest.cy.ts`: text field initializers. The spec is skipped today, see [Jahia/jcontent#2168](https://github.com/Jahia/jcontent/issues/2168).

## Leftover setup to remove

These specs enable the legacy page composer in their `before` hook but never open it. Remove the `jcontent/enableLegacyPageComposer.graphql` call.

- [ ] `tests/cypress/e2e/pickers/pickerMultiple.cy.ts`
- [ ] `tests/cypress/e2e/pickers/search.cy.ts`
- [ ] `tests/cypress/e2e/selectorTypes/validation.cy.ts`
- [ ] The rest of `previewContent.cy.ts`, `deleteAdvanced.cy.ts` and `editorUrl.cy.ts` once their page composer tests have moved.

## Out of scope

- `tests/cypress/e2e/jcontent/shard2/links.cy.ts`, the test `Trying to access legacy page composer redirect to page builder`, stays in jcontent: it tests the redirect behind the jcontent `hideLegacyPageComposer` setting.
- `tests/cypress/e2e/pageBuilder/*` tests the jcontent Page Builder, not the legacy page composer. The fixtures it reads under `tests/cypress/fixtures/jcontent/pageComposer/` keep their place, though a rename to `pageBuilder/` would remove the confusion.

## Cleanup in jcontent once the tests have moved

- [ ] Remove `tests/cypress/page-object/pageComposer.ts`, `tests/cypress/page-object/pageComposerContextualMenu.ts` and their exports from `tests/cypress/page-object/index.ts`, unless the redirect test of `links.cy.ts` still needs `PageComposer.visit`.
- [ ] Remove `tests/cypress/fixtures/jcontent/enableLegacyPageComposer.graphql` if nothing reads it any more.
- [ ] Decide whether `tests/provisioning-manifest-snapshot.yml` still needs `mvn:org.jahia.modules/jahia-page-composer`, which depends on whether the redirect test of `links.cy.ts` needs the module installed.
title: Migrate legacy page composer Cypress tests to jahia-page-composer

I did not check whether `EmailInput` is used; the grep for kit inputs found none in `src`.

## Expected behavior

No Russian text visible anywhere in the running app. Tests and docs match the English UI.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] All user-visible strings listed above are English, including alt texts and placeholders.
- [ ] A local date component replaces the kit's `FormattedDate` in `order-card.tsx` and `order-info.tsx`.
- [ ] Kit components with Russian defaults (`PasswordInput`) get explicit English `placeholder` and `errorText`.
- [ ] `public/index.html` has `lang="en"`.
- [ ] Cypress test and `cypress/fixtures/ingredients.json` updated to English strings and passing.
- [ ] Jest tests and Storybook stories updated to English and passing.
- [ ] Russian TODO comments translated, or removed if obsolete.
- [ ] `README.md` rewritten in English (or reduced to what this project needs).
- [ ] Re-run the Cyrillic search over `src cypress public README.md` and it returns nothing.
title: Translate the whole UI to English

Suite: `packages/ui-tests/cypress/e2e/datamapper/xpath-editor.cy.ts`

[data-testid^="node-source-"]
Queried from: cy.get(.source-panel)
```

The suite reports 1 setup failure and skips the remaining 9 tests. XPath interactions are therefore not covered by this run.

Use development mode: this suite needs the DataMapper debug menu, which is absent from the production build.

In another terminal:

env -u ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE yarn workspace @kaoto/kaoto-tests exec cypress run \

- [ ] Determine whether schema attachment updates the source document successfully.
- [ ] Inspect tree population, panel expansion/dimensions, and virtualized row rendering.

A church staff member imports a spreadsheet where people in the same household share a `FamilyID` and expects one family per household. Today no CI test asserts that.

## What to add

A new test in `cypress/e2e/ui-admin/admin.csvimport.spec.js` (or a new spec beside it) with its own fixture in `cypress/fixtures/`. The fixture has several `FamilyID`s. After the import, check:

- Rows that share a `FamilyID` land in one family.
- Different `FamilyID`s create separate families.
- The family's name and address come from its rows.
- A row with no `FamilyID` gets its own family.

Delete the imported records in `after()` the way the existing spec does (distinctive `LastName`, then `cy.cleanupFamilies` / `cy.cleanupPeople`).

- Import flow and mapping: `src/admin/routes/api/import.php`, `src/admin/views/csv-import.php`
- Existing spec to copy from: `cypress/e2e/ui-admin/admin.csvimport.spec.js` (the "sets custom fields and properties" test already resolves a family through `/api/person/{id}` → `FamId` and `/api/family/{id}`)

- It fails if the importer stops grouping by `FamilyID`.
- It leaves no families or people behind.

  - 3.3: none (code)
- **Introduced** `pkp/pkp-lib#11765` (for `pkp/pkp-lib#857` by its branch name) · [52d3a0f8e7](https://github.com/pkp/pkp-lib/commit/52d3a0f8e70659ff8a1507068866a6abdeb8ec90) · 2025-11-11, merged 2025-11-20 · jyhein (jyhein)
- **Upstream** none found (2026-10-01)
- **Tracked in** spec U63 [OMP4](https://github.com/jardakotesovec/pkp-e2e/blob/main/docs/specs/U63-import-export.md#omp4)
- **Checked** 2026-10-01, each branch's tip (the commits in Evidence)
- **Model** claude-opus-5-5

## Summary

A press loads monographs in bulk with "Tab Delimited Content Import
Plugin", which runs only from the server's command line. With the
plugin's own sample file, the tool stops with a PHP fatal error at the
first author, before any import message. No monograph is imported, and
the rows after that one are never read.

Each run also leaves a new submission with no title, no author and no
file. It sits at the top of the editors' "Active submissions" as
"Incomplete". A press manager can delete it, and the monographs can be
entered another way.

Only the development line has the fault; no release does. Every file
fails at its first row that names an author.

## Impact

- **Lost.** The whole import, and the time spent preparing the file.
  Nobody is told why beyond the PHP error.
- **Who.** Whoever runs the tool on the server for a press: today a
  developer or tester on `main`, after the next release any press that
  bulk-loads titles with it.
- **Way round.** The Native XML Plugin imports monographs, from Tools
  or from its own command line, and "Start A New Submission" enters one
  title at a time. The Dashboard's "Delete Incomplete Submissions"
  removes the empty submissions.

Medium: the tool fails on every file with a fatal error and leaves an
empty submission behind, but it is a bulk shortcut with other ways in.

## Steps to reproduce

Preconditions:

- PKP's default test dataset for `main` (OMP), press `publicknowledge`.
- A shell in the OMP directory of that install.
- A file `u63ir22.csv`: the plugin's own
  `plugins/importexport/csv/sample.csv` with its title replaced by
  "Monograph u63ir22", and its `submission.pdf`, which the OMP tree
  lacks, replaced by `cypress/fixtures/dummy.pdf`:

  ```
  pressPath,authorString,title,abstract,seriesPath,year,isEditedVolume,locale,filename,doi
  publicknowledge,Author1 Surname1<author@pkp.sfu.ca>;Author2 Surname2<author2@sfu.pkp.ca>,Monograph u63ir22,Abstract text,,2024,1,en,cypress/fixtures/dummy.pdf,https://doi.org/10.1111/hex.12487
  ```

Steps:

1. Sign in as `dbarnes`. The Dashboard's side menu reads "16 Active
   submissions" and "2 Published".
2. From the OMP directory, run
   `php tools/importExport.php CSVImportExportPlugin u63ir22.csv admin`.
3. On the Dashboard, open "Published".
4. Search for "Monograph u63ir22". Press "View" on the row found, then
   "Contributors".
5. Open "Active submissions" and look at the top row.

**Expected.** Step 2 prints:

```
Submission: 'Monograph u63ir22' successfully imported.
```

In step 3, "Published" counts 3 and lists "Surname1 et al. — Monograph
u63ir22". Step 4 finds that row, "Published", and its Contributors list
"Author1 Surname1" and "Author2 Surname2", each "Author". Step 5 shows
no new row.

**Observed.** Step 2 ends in a PHP fatal error with exit status 255,
before any import message. Where the error shows depends on the PHP
command line's `display_errors`. With it off, as on the walked install,
standard output stays empty and the error stream reads:

```
PHP Fatal error:  Uncaught Error: Call to undefined method APP\author\Author::setUserGroupId() in …/plugins/importexport/csv/CSVImportExportPlugin.php:220
```

With it on (PHP's development `php.ini`), the same error goes to
standard output as `Fatal error: Uncaught Error: Call to undefined
method APP\author\Author::setUserGroupId() …`.

"Published" still counts 2, and step 4 shows "Search Results (0)" and
"No Items". In step 5, "Active submissions" now counts 17, and its top
row reads "19", "Incomplete", with no title and no author, and a
"Complete submission" button. That button opens "Make a Submission:
Upload Files" for submission 19, with no file.

## Cause

`CSVImportExportPlugin::executeCLI()` (OMP,
`plugins/importexport/csv/CSVImportExportPlugin.php`) builds each
author with `$author->setUserGroupId($authorGroup->id)` (line 220).
52d3a0f8e7, "Contributor Roles and Type", replaced an author's user
group with a contributor type and contributor roles, and removed
`Author::setUserGroupId()` and `getUserGroupId()`. The OMP side of that
change, `pkp/omp#2164`, updated the press's own classes and tests, but
not this plugin, so the call now ends the script.

When that line fails, the row's import is half done.
`Repo::submission()->add()` has already stored the submission and its
first version. The status, stage and the other fields are set on the
objects before the author loop (lines 186 to 192) but saved only after
it (lines 232 and 233), and the title is set only after it (line 231).
So the new submission keeps the defaults of `add()`: "Incomplete"
(`submission_progress` "start"), in the submission stage, with no
title. The authors, the "PDF" format and the file are never written.

Reach:

- Every file: the run stops at the first row whose author string
  matches the plugin's name pattern, and the rows after it are never
  read. A row whose authors all fail the pattern is skipped as
  "invalid author" and imported with no author. Walked for the sample
  row; the rest read in the code.
- No other code in OJS, OMP or OPS calls `setUserGroupId()` or
  `getUserGroupId()` on an author: checked in the code (the three apps'
  `classes`, `pages`, `plugins` and their `lib/pkp`). The QuickSubmit
  plugin had the same call and was fixed under `pkp/pkp-lib#12179`.
- The web: nothing, since the tool has no page of its own (its Tools
  link is `pkp/pkp-lib#8785`).

## Proposed fix

Give each imported author the press's "Author" contributor role, as
`Repo::author()->newAuthorFromUser()` does for a submitting author, and
look the role up where the plugin looked up the author group. This is
[fix.diff](https://github.com/jardakotesovec/pkp-e2e/blob/main/shared/playwright/checks/issues/command-line-csv-import-empty-submission/fix.diff),
one file in OMP:

```diff
-            $authorGroup = UserGroup::withContextIds([$press->getId()])
-                ->withRoleIds([Role::ROLE_ID_AUTHOR])
-                ->isDefault(true)
-                ->get()
+            $authorRole = ContributorRole::query()
+                ->withContextId($press->getId())
+                ->withIdentifier(ContributorRoleIdentifier::AUTHOR->getName())
                 ->first();
-            if (!$authorGroup) {
+            if (!$authorRole) {
 …
-                $author->setUserGroupId($authorGroup->id);
+                $author->setData('contributorType', ContributorType::PERSON->getName());
+                $author->setContributorRoles([$authorRole]);
```

with the three `use` lines for `ContributorRole`,
`ContributorRoleIdentifier` and `ContributorType` in place of `Role`
and `UserGroup`. The type line matches `newAuthorFromUser()`; PERSON is
also the `contributor_type` column's default
(`lib/pkp/classes/migration/install/SubmissionsMigration.php`, line
118), so the role is the line that matters. The Native XML import's
author filter (`NativeXmlPKPAuthorFilter`) falls back to the same
"Author" role the same way.

Tried on `main`: step 2 prints the Expected line, step 4 finds the
monograph with its two authors, each "Author", and step 5 shows no new
row. "Published" still counts 2: see the stage below. A row naming a
press the site lacks is still skipped with `Unknown Press:
"nosuchpress".  Skipping.` and adds nothing, with the fix in and out.

**Alternatives**

- Bring back `setUserGroupId()` on `Author` as a deprecated shim. It
  would store a value nothing reads any more, and the authors would
  have no role.
- Drop the `setUserGroupId()` line alone. The type falls back to the
  column's default, but the authors get no role, which the contributor
  form does not allow.

**What goes with it**

- The stage. The plugin marks the submission published and sets it to
  "Production", but never publishes its version, which reads "Status:
  Unscheduled" (on 3.5 too). On `main`, a submission moves to the new
  "Done" stage when a version is published (`ApplyDoneWorkflowStage`,
  on `PublicationPublished`), and "Published" lists that stage only. So
  even with the fix, the monograph is not counted in "Published" on
  `main`. The same change should decide this, for example by
  publishing the version through `Repo::publication()->publish()`
  instead of setting the status. Not tried.
- The empty submission comes from the plugin writing a row in several
  saves. Wrapping each row in a database transaction would make any
  later failure leave nothing behind. Not tried.
- The message `plugins.importexport.csv.noAuthorGroup` ("There is no
  default author group in the press …") now answers a missing "Author"
  role. Its wording could follow.
- No stored data to repair, and no API or hook change.
- Guard: a PHPUnit test in OMP that runs `executeCLI()` on a CSV file
  of its own with a PDF fixture, since `sample.csv` names a
  `submission.pdf` the OMP tree lacks, and that stays off the error
  paths, which call `exit`. It reads back the title and the two
  authors with their role.

Small: a few lines in one OMP file, and a unit test.

## 结论

`ms-toollib@1.6.1` 中新增的 RMV `version_info` 白名单漏掉了合法版本字符串 `Vienna Minesweeper - Scoreganizer Client Edition - Release 3.0.2C`。因此 1.6.0 可正常解析的 RMV 录像，在 1.6.1 中会被 `RmvVideo::parse()` 判为 `ErrReadVideoReason::InvalidParams`；WASM 包装层随后在 `unwrap()` panic 后调用 `free()`，又产生 `attempted to take ownership of Rust value while it was borrowed` 的次生错误。

上游 open-minesweeper 的 Dependabot PR #1319 将 npm `ms-toollib` 从 1.6.0 提升到 1.6.1 后暴露了此回归：

- CI 作业：https://github.com/eee555/open-minesweeper/actions/runs/42887053130/job/130078027683?pr=1319
- 失败录像：`front_end/cypress/fixtures/3819-Time-1616-NF-9469-32-20151031.rmv`（来自 open-minesweeper PR #1319 提交 `34f2f7d`）
- Vitest：4 failed / 877 passed；`counter.test.ts`、`exportReplayState.test.ts`、`mouseTrace.test.ts`、`useReplayPosition.test.ts` 都只在该 RMV 用例失败。
- Cypress 组件测试：`VideoUpload/App.cy.ts` 中该 RMV 的状态变为 `Cannot parse the file`。其他分片失败（如 `GSCAdmin/HistoryVideos.cy.ts`）未显示与 ms-toollib 有关，不纳入本结论。

## 最小复现

下载发布包 `ms-toollib@1.6.0` 与 `ms-toollib@1.6.1`，使用上述 RMV 文件执行等价逻辑：

```js
const video = new RmvVideo(new Uint8Array(bytes), '3819-Time-1616-NF-9469-32-20151031.rmv');
try {
  video.parse();
  console.log('ok', video.rtime_ms, video.bbbv);
  video.free();
} catch (error) {
  // 前端 replayParser.ts 的异常清理路径
  video.free();
  throw error;
}
```

本地 Node.js 27 实测：

| 版本 | `parse()` | `free()` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1.6.0 | 成功：`rtime_ms=9469`、`bbbv=32` | 成功 |
| 1.6.1 | WASM panic：`called Result::unwrap() on an Err value: InvalidParams`，JS 抛出 `unreachable` | 抛出 `attempted to take ownership of Rust value while it was borrowed` |

CI 日志中的原始 panic 是：

```text
panicked at src/board.rs:956:1:
called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: InvalidParams
  at RmvVideo.parse (.../ms_toollib_bg.js:4417:14)
```

随后 Vitest 报告：

```text
Error: attempted to take ownership of Rust value while it was borrowed
  at RmvVideo.free (.../ms_toollib_bg.js:3809:14)
  at parseReplay (.../replayParser.ts:22:15)
```

## 根因

测试录像中的 `version_info` 原文为：

```text
Vienna Minesweeper - Scoreganizer Client Edition - Release 3.0.2C Copyright ...（版权所有者部分以原始二进制为准）
```

按 `base/src/videos/rmv_video.rs` 的版权尾部截断规则，规范化后的版本字符串是：

```text
Vienna Minesweeper - Scoreganizer Client Edition - Release 3.0.2C
```

但发布提交 `d8abf43` 的白名单只登记了：

- `base/src/videos/rmv_video.rs:430`：`Vienna Minesweeper - Scoreganizer Client Edition - Release 3.0C`
- `base/src/videos/rmv_video.rs:434`：未匹配时直接 `return Err(ErrReadVideoReason::InvalidParams)`

`3.0.2C` 不在该列表中。`version_info` 的读取和严格白名单由提交 `3b41c39` 引入，随后包含在 1.6.1 发布中；1.6.0 发布提交 `fe5d573` 仍直接跳过 `version_info`，所以没有此问题。

另有相关问题：`base/src/videos/base_video.rs` 的 `valid_time_period()` 也只登记 `Release 3.0C`，没有 `3.0H`、`3.0.2H`、`3.0.2C`；即使补上 parse 白名单，这些版本在 `is_valid()` 的版本有效期检查里仍会走 `Unknown software` 分支。建议两处白名单一起核对。

WASM 侧的二次错误来自 `wasm/src/board.rs:600` 的 `self.core.parse().unwrap()`。当 Rust 解析返回 `Err` 时 panic 发生在 `&mut self` 的 wasm-bindgen 借期内；调用方 `replayParser.ts` 在 catch 中继续 `video.free()`，于是触发 wasm-bindgen 的 borrow/ownership 检查。它是首因的衍生症状，但使真实错误信息被 `unreachable` 和借用错误掩盖。

## 建议

1. 将 `Vienna Minesweeper - Scoreganizer Client Edition - Release 3.0.2C` 加入 RMV `version_info` 白名单，并同步补入 `valid_time_period()`；核对 `3.0H` / `3.0.2H` 的有效期表。
2. 为所有已登记的历史 Vienna 版本增加 `parse()` 回归测试，至少覆盖该 RMV 测试文件，避免再次因白名单遗漏拒绝旧录像。
3. 考虑让未知但结构合法的 `version_info` 降级为“保留原始字符串 + 标记非官方/待复核”，而不是直接拒绝解析；否则每出现一个历史版本都会形成破坏性回归。
4. WASM `parse()` 应把 `Result` 映射为可捕获的 JS 异常并避免 panic 后留下悬空 borrow；这样异常清理路径中的 `free()` 不会覆盖原始错误。

## 环境

- npm `ms-toollib` 1.6.0 / 1.6.1（1.6.1 tarball integrity：`sha512-RZ7i3f3vMaMyBzgy+mZhF3a6XwOhcG+/Xd8wwtEveOAGxzxcOiDKTEHNEpe3WvNEQs3Qheb/A0ooBWWrbpEBPA==`）
- open-minesweeper PR #1319，提交 `34f2f7d`，Node.js 24（CI）；本地复核使用 Node.js 27
- 源码版本：发布提交 `d8abf43`；回归引入提交 `3b41c39`

## Bug Report

Some CALM Hub seed data and one CALM Hub UI fixture still use the 2024-04 and 2024-10 drafts. Both drafts were removed long ago, so every one of these URLs gives 404. Step 6 of #3240 removes the references to the drafts. The PR for the 2026-03 draft leaves these, because each document needs a release that it is valid against, as in #3469.

### Context / Problem to solve / Design An administrator who adds HTML filtering to a platform with existing content needs to measure that content before the module changes or refuses anything. The HTML filtering report of [Jahia/html-filtering#189](https://github.com/Jahia/html-filtering/issues/189) gives that measurement, but the module must be installed for the report to run. The module enforces its rules as soon as it starts. The global default configuration sets `REJECT` for `editWorkspace` and `SANITIZE` for `liveWorkspace`, and `strategy` accepts only these two values. A configuration with another value fails the validation, and the module then uses the next configuration in the priority chain. No configuration today keeps the module installed without validation or sanitization. This story adds a third strategy, `DISABLED`. A workspace with this strategy is not validated and not sanitized on save. The rules of the policy stay available to the report and to the GraphQL `validate` query. ### Story As a server administrator, I want to set the strategy of a workspace to `DISABLED`, So that I can install HTML filtering and run the report before the module rejects or sanitizes any content. ### Scope - `strategy` accepts `DISABLED` in `editWorkspace` and in `liveWorkspace`, at each configuration level: site, global custom and global default. The value is case-insensitive, as the other values are today. - With `DISABLED`, a save in that workspace keeps the HTML unchanged: - The interceptor does not sanitize the value. - The validator does not reject the content. - With `DISABLED`, the rules of the policy still apply to: - the GraphQL `validate` query, - the HTML filtering report of [Jahia/html-filtering#189](https://github.com/Jahia/html-filtering/issues/189). - The module logs a warning when it loads a configuration with `DISABLED` in a workspace. The warning names the configuration and the workspace, because that workspace has no XSS protection from the module. - The priority chain does not change. A site configuration with `REJECT` overrides a global custom configuration with `DISABLED` for that site. - The global default configuration does not change: `REJECT` in `editWorkspace` and `SANITIZE` in `liveWorkspace`. - `docs/html-filtering.md` describes `DISABLED` in the Strategy section. It also gives the procedure to install the module with `DISABLED` and run the report before any enforcement. ### Testable scenarios ```gherkin Background: Given a global custom configuration with strategy DISABLED in editWorkspace and in liveWorkspace And its allowedRuleSet allows

and does not allow in the default workspace Then the save succeeds And the stored value is

text

Scenario: A save in the live workspace keeps the HTML unchanged When a user saves a rich text property with

text

in the live workspace Then the save succeeds And the stored value is

text

Scenario: The publication keeps the HTML unchanged Given a content in the default workspace with

text

When an editor publishes the content Then the value in the live workspace is

text

Scenario: The GraphQL validate query still applies the rules When the GraphQL validate query runs on

text

for the site Then removedTags contains script And safe is false Scenario: The report still applies the rules Given a content with

text

in a rich text property When a site administrator runs the HTML filtering report Then the report lists the content with the markup Then the save fails with the HTML filtering error Scenario: The module logs a warning When the module loads the global custom configuration Then the log contains a warning that names the global custom configuration and the workspaces editWorkspace and liveWorkspace ``` ### Test Strategy - Cypress tests for the scenarios above, with configuration fixtures as in `tests/cypress/fixtures/configs/`. The scenario of the report runs when [Jahia/html-filtering#189](https://github.com/Jahia/html-filtering/issues/189) is merged. - Unit tests in `ConfigBuilderTest` for the new value, in upper case and in lower case. ### Tech Notes - The two enforcement points already select their strategy. `HtmlFilteringInterceptor` resolves the policy with `Strategy.SANITIZE`, and `HtmlValidator` resolves it with `Strategy.REJECT`. A policy with `DISABLED` therefore matches neither, and neither class needs a change. - The change is in three places: - the `Strategy` enum, - the `PolicyModel.PolicyStrategy` enum, - the `switch` of `ConfigBuilder.readStrategy`. - `Strategy` is in `org.jahia.modules.htmlfiltering`, which is an exported package. A new constant is binary compatible, but a module that switches on `Strategy` must handle `DISABLED`. State this in the changelog. - The GraphQL `validate` query calls `PolicyResolver.resolvePolicy(siteKey, workspace)` without a strategy, so `DISABLED` does not change its result. The report of [Jahia/html-filtering#189](https://github.com/Jahia/html-filtering/issues/189) must resolve the policy the same way. - The configuration `skip: ['nt:base']` turns off the enforcement today. It is not a replacement for `DISABLED`, because the report applies the same `skip` rule and then finds no property to check. - Check the installation order. The procedure in the documentation puts `org.jahia.modules.htmlfiltering.global.custom.yml` with `DISABLED` in place before the module starts. A test must show that no save is sanitized or rejected between the start of the module and the load of that configuration. - HTML filtering v1 had the option `htmlSanitizerDryRun`, which v2 removed. `DISABLED` covers a part of that need. - Ship this strategy in the same minor version as [Jahia/html-filtering#189](https://github.com/Jahia/html-filtering/issues/189).
title: Add a DISABLED strategy that neither validates nor sanitizes content

`pnpm run test:e2e` fails under CPU load because each e2e test spawns the full CLI and has a fixed per-test timeout of 20-30 s. A rerun on an idle machine passes. Next step: pick one fix option below.

## Symptom

Under load, a different set of CLI-spawning tests times out on each run. The same tests take 3.5-5 s each on an idle machine.

## Measurements (macOS arm64, 14 cores)

Load: 14 `yes > /dev/null` processes (one per core), killed after each run.

| Test | Timeout | Idle | Loaded |
|---|---|---|---|
| e2e-cli-rules > detects focused test in Cypress fixture TodoList.cy.ts via CLI | 30 s | 3.6-4.2 s | 28.9 s pass, 31.8 s fail |
| e2e-cli-rules > detects missing assertion in Cypress fixture TodoListAssertionFree.cy.ts via CLI | 30 s | 3.7-4.1 s | 35.2 s fail |
| e2e-cli-rules > passes cleanly on Cypress fixture TodoListClean.cy.ts via CLI | 30 s | 3.8-4.3 s | 45.6 s fail |
| e2e-cli-rules > passes cleanly on Cypress fixture TodoListLookalike.cy.ts via CLI | 30 s | 3.8-4.3 s | 33.5 s fail |
| e2e-cli-rules > detects stale-mock-export in stale.test.ts | 30 s | 4.1-5.0 s | 63.1 s fail |
| e2e-cli-rules > detects React, hooks, perf, effect, and compiler rules in react-components.tsx | 20 s | 3.8-3.9 s | 62.1 s fail |
| e2e-cli-rules > detects unused-export and unused-file in dead-code directory | 30 s | | 54.5 s fail |
| e2e-cli-rules > detects strict-mode in tsconfig.json via CLI sandbox | 30 s | | 76.1 s fail |
| e2e-synthetic > detects all Evil Martians categories on a synthetic repository | 25 s | | 38.2 s, 258.2 s fail |
| cli > outputs structured JSON when --json is passed | 30 s | | 34.3 s, 101.1 s fail |
| cli > outputs Markdown findings when --llm is passed | 30 s | | 245.3 s fail |

Full idle suite: 40/40 passed in 131 s. Loaded full-suite runs did not finish within 6 minutes.

## Configured timeouts

- `vitest.e2e.config.ts:13`: `testTimeout: 60000` (overridden per test)
- `tests/e2e-cli-rules.test.ts`: per-test `30000` on most tests (for example `:182`, `:190`, `:194`, `:198`, `:204`, `:214`), `20000` at `:220` (duplication) and `:304` (React)
- `tests/cli.test.ts:41`, `:50`: `30000`
- `tests/e2e-synthetic.test.ts:133`: `25000`

## Cause

- Each test runs `node bin/anti-slop` through `execSync` (`tests/e2e-cli-rules.test.ts:30-33`, `tests/cli.test.ts:33`, `:44`). Every spawn builds a fresh ESLint and TypeScript program.
- The suite uses `pool: "threads"` (`vitest.e2e.config.ts:12`), so the three files spawn CLIs in parallel and compete with each other as well as with any outside load.
- `execSync` blocks the worker. vitest cannot stop the child at the timeout; it marks the test as failed when the call returns. That is why the durations above are well past the limits.
- The fixed limits leave about 5-8x headroom over idle time. Machine load (mutation runs, other worktrees, CI neighbours) uses up that headroom.

## Fix options

1. **Remove the per-test overrides** so the config's 60 s applies, or raise it further. Smallest change. It hides slowness rather than removing it, and a stuck CLI takes longer to report.
2. **Run each fixture directory once** in a `beforeAll` (or one CLI call over all fixtures), and have the tests assert on the shared JSON. This removes most of the spawns and the contention, but the tests become coupled to one run, so one crash fails many tests.
3. **Limit e2e parallelism** (`fileParallelism: false` or `maxWorkers: 1` in `vitest.e2e.config.ts`). This removes self-contention and gives stable timings, but the idle suite gets slower.

Options 2 and 3 can be combined. Option 1 alone is enough if the goal is only to stop false failures.

## Acceptance

`pnpm run test:e2e` passes three runs in a row with one `yes` process per core running, and the idle wall time does not grow by more than the chosen option implies.
title: test(e2e): stop CLI e2e tests timing out under CPU load

Als Betreiber will ich weitere Eingabefelder zur Lieferung definieren können, damit diese als Metadaten erfasst werden können.

**Entscheide:**
- Die festen Felder "Vorgänger", "Teillieferung" und "Kommentar" bleiben, wie sie sind. Die neuen Felder kommen daneben; die Vorgänger-Lieferung wird kein eigener Eingabetyp.
- Metadaten sind echte Metadaten: rein informativ, ohne fachliche Logik. geopilot prüft, ob ein Wert vorhanden ist und die richtige Form hat, wertet ihn aber nicht aus. Ein Feld mit einer Rolle bleibt ein eigenes Feld: Der Vorgänger verweist auf eine andere Lieferung, die Teillieferung hat Logik zusammen mit dem Vorgänger, und der Kommentar ist die Beschreibung der Lieferung, im STAC-Item das Standardfeld `description`. Soll ein Metadatum einmal Verhalten steuern, wird daraus ein eigenes Feld.
- Eine Lieferung speichert eine Kopie der Felddefinitionen samt Wert. Ändert sich das Mandat später (Feld umbenannt, entfernt, neu Pflicht), bleiben bestehende Lieferungen unverändert.
- Geprüft wird nur bei der Lieferung, gegen die Felder, die das Mandat in diesem Moment hat.

**Dabei:**
- Konfiguration pro Mandat in der Mandatsmaske unter "Lieferformular", Abschnitt "Weitere Felder": pro Feld eine Id, ein mehrsprachiger Titel, ein Typ und die Checkbox "Pflichtfeld".
- Eingabetypen: Text, Liste von Texten, Auswahl (genau eine der vom Admin vorgegebenen Optionen, mehrsprachig), Zahl ohne Nachkommastellen, Zahl mit Nachkommastellen, Datum.
- Eingabe ist beim Abschluss der Lieferung möglich, nach den festen Feldern (wie bisher z.B. ein Kommentar).
- Maschinelle Lieferung: Die Werte kommen als `metadata` mit der Id als Schlüssel, auf der JSON-Route als Objekt, auf der Multipart-Route als Formularfeld vor den Dateien. Die Ids gehören damit zum Vertrag mit den Clients (`docs/MaschinelleAnlieferung.md`).
- Anzeige: auf der Lieferdetailseite der Administration, im STAC-Item (nur für Admins, wie der Kommentar) und im Mail-Template über den Platzhalter `{{metadata}}` bzw. `{{metadata:de}}`.

**Abgrenzungen:**
- Der Inhalt von Text-Feldern wird nicht ausgewertet (ausser dass Pflichtfelder ausgefüllt wurden).
- Keine Mehrfachauswahl, kein Minimum, Maximum oder Muster für Zahlen und Texte.
- Kein Schalter pro Feld für die Sichtbarkeit im öffentlichen STAC-Katalog; kann nachträglich kommen.
- Keine Metadaten in der Ablage, in der Lieferübersicht der Lieferanten, in Pipeline-Bedingungen oder in einer Suche.

**Szenarien:**

Szenario 1 (Lieferung im Web):
1. Prozessierung durchführen
2. Zum Abschluss der Lieferung dürfen / müssen die Eingabefelder des Mandats ausgefüllt werden
3. Die Werte erscheinen auf der Lieferdetailseite, im STAC-Item für Admins und in der Info-Mail

Szenario 2 (maschinelle Lieferung):
1. Ein Client liefert mit `metadata`
2. Fehlt ein Pflichtfeld, passt ein Wert nicht zum Typ oder ist eine Id unbekannt, antwortet geopilot mit `400` unter `metadata.<id>`, bevor die Verarbeitung beginnt

Szenario 3 (Mandat ändert sich):
1. Ein Admin benennt ein Feld um, entfernt es oder macht es zur Pflicht
2. Bestehende Lieferungen behalten ihre Kopie unverändert
3. Ein Versuch einer maschinellen Lieferung, dessen Werte nicht mehr passen, scheitert bei der automatischen Deklaration und muss neu eingereicht werden

Umsetzung in #1186, die Smoke-Tests stehen im Kommentar unten.
title: Weitere Eingabefelder zur Lieferung

@DawoudIO, a request about the "Injection and escaping" pre-merge check in `.coderabbit.yaml` (#10327). It fails any PR that adds SQL anywhere in the diff, including:

- **Schema scripts.** `src/mysql/upgrade/*.sql` and `src/mysql/install/Install.sql` are the only way to add a table, and "Schema upgrade safety" requires them. #10392 passes that check and then fails this one on the same `CREATE TABLE` statements.
- **Seed data.** `cypress/data/seed.sql`.
- **Cypress fixtures.** `cy.dbQuery()` calls in specs, all with bound parameters. The repo already has many of them, and #10360 fails the same way.

It currently blocks #10360, #10378, #10379, #10381, #10382, #10384, #10389 and #10392.

**Proposal:** keep the check as it is for application code, and exempt `src/mysql/` and `cypress/`:

```yaml
      - name: Injection and escaping
        mode: error
        instructions: |
          Fail if the PR adds RunQuery() or raw SQL in application code, concatenates
          request input into a query, or prints request or database values into HTML
          or script without InputUtils escaping. SQL under src/mysql/ (install and
          upgrade scripts) and cypress/ (seed data and cy.dbQuery test fixtures) does
          not count.
```

## Feature Proposal

### Target Project:
`calm-hub-ui`, `calm-hub`, `cli`

### Description of Feature:
Let an organisation add features to CALM Hub without a fork. An extension is a package that declares what it adds, where it appears in the UI and API, and which commands it provides. One extension manifest drives both the UI and the CLI, so that people, scripts and AI agents use the same capability.

Today every screen and tab is compiled into the UI. For example, the `Diagram / JSON / Deployments` tabs are fixed in `DiagramSection.tsx`, and the landing page sections are fixed in the intro screen.

### User Stories:
- As a platform team, I want to add a screen to Hub, so that my users find our internal tool in one place.
- As an architect, I want extra tabs next to Diagram and JSON, so that I see deployments, cost or risk for the same architecture.
- As an operator, I want to turn extensions on or off per environment, so that I control what users see.
- As an automation or AI agent author, I want the same extension features from the CLI, so that I do not need to drive a browser.

### Current Limitations:
- No way to add a screen, tab, card or search handler without a change to Hub itself.
- `Deployments` is a built-in tab, so it cannot be a worked example for others.
- The search box only runs the built-in catalogue search.
- The CLI cannot discover or call features that a Hub deployment adds.

### Proposed Implementation:

#### Extension points

| Extension point | What the user sees | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `screen` | A new top-level page, linked from the hamburger menu | Gets its own route, `/ext/<id>` |
| `designer-tab` | A tab beside Diagram and JSON in the architecture view | Diagram and JSON stay built in. `Deployments` moves to an extension and is the first example |
| `landing-card` | A section beside NAMESPACES and CONTROL DOMAINS on the landing page | Card shows a title, a count or summary, and a link |
| `chat` | An AI assistant, opened from the "Search architecture catalogue" box | Only one chat provider is active at a time |
| `search-provider` | Extra result groups in global search | Chat and search share one entry point |
| `detail-panel` | A panel in the node, control or flow side drawer | For example, ownership or runtime status |
| `action` | A button in a toolbar or menu (export, publish, open in tool) | Same action is a CLI command |

#### Design points

| Topic | Proposal |
|---|---|
| Manifest | One JSON file per extension: `id`, `version`, `contributes` (extension points), `permissions`, `commands`. A JSON Schema validates it |
| Registry | Hub reads manifests from config at start up and serves them from a new `GET /calm/extensions` endpoint. Hub UI and CLI both read it |
| UI loading | Lazy-loaded remote module, loaded only when its extension point is shown. A failing extension must not break the host page. Use an error boundary per slot |
| UI contract | Typed props for each extension point (the selected architecture, version, namespace, theme). Put the types in a shared package so authors do not import Hub internals |
| Backend | An extension can ship a REST route set or call an external service. Hub proxies it behind the same auth. No new auth path |
| Auth | Extensions get the user's token through the host, never their own login. Manifest `permissions` are shown to the operator and checked by Hub |
| Config | Enable, disable and order per environment in Hub config. Extends the existing `UiConfig` |
| CLI | `calm extensions list`, `calm extensions describe <id>`, and `calm ext <id> <command>`. The CLI reads the manifest `commands` and calls the same Hub API. JSON output by default for scripts |
| AI and automation | Manifest commands carry a JSON Schema for input and output. Hub exposes them through the existing MCP server in `calm-hub`, so an agent finds them with no extra code |
| Chat contract | Extension receives the query and catalogue context and streams a reply. Hub owns the UI shell, the extension owns the model and prompts |
| Theming | Extensions use Hub's DaisyUI tokens so light and dark mode work |

#### Delivery plan

1. Manifest schema, registry endpoint and UI slot component (no extension yet).
2. Move `Deployments` to a `designer-tab` extension. This proves the model with no change for users.
3. `screen` and `landing-card` points.
4. CLI commands and MCP exposure.
5. `chat` point, with a reference extension.

Each step is its own PR.

### Alternatives Considered:

| Option | Why not |
|---|---|
| Fork Hub per organisation | Fork drift, no shared upgrade path |
| Build all features into Hub with feature flags | Hub then holds every organisation's needs. Maintainers carry that cost |
| iframe only | Simple and isolated, but weak theme, auth and navigation integration. Can remain an option for `screen` |
| UI-only extensions | Leaves automation and AI agents without access. Rejected as a base design |

### Open Questions:
- Module Federation, native ES modules with import maps, or web components for UI loading? Needs a spike.
- Trust model: are extensions only operator-installed, or can a user add one? Proposal is operator-only.
- How do extensions get versioned against the Hub UI contract?
- Should the first CLI step wait for a stable manifest, or ship `list` and `describe` early?

### Testing Strategy:
- Unit tests: manifest validation (valid and invalid), registry endpoint, slot rendering, error boundary on a failing extension.
- Existing `DiagramSection` tests keep passing after `Deployments` moves.
- Cypress test with a small fixture extension for each extension point.
- CLI tests for `list`, `describe` and command dispatch against a mock Hub.

### Documentation Requirements:
- Extension author guide, with a minimal example per extension point.
- Manifest schema reference.
- Operator guide for enable, disable and permissions.
- Update `calm-hub-ui/AGENTS.md`, `calm-hub/AGENTS.md` and `cli/AGENTS.md`.

### Implementation Checklist:
- [ ] Design reviewed and approved
- [ ] Implementation completed
- [ ] Tests written and passing
- [ ] Documentation updated
- [ ] Relevant workflows updated (if needed)
- [ ] Performance impact assessed

### Additional Context:
Related code: `calm-hub-ui/src/hub/components/diagram-section/DiagramSection.tsx` (tabs), `calm-hub-ui/src/hub/components/intro-screen/` (landing page), `calm-hub-ui/src/components/navbar/` (menu and search), `calm-hub-ui/src/model/ui-config.ts` (config), `calm-hub/.../mcp` (MCP server).

## Problem

Observed while validating #3557, not introduced by its product changes. `CI=true pnpm verify:prepush` passed the routed unit suite, 926 presentation tests, the disposable PostgreSQL proof (3 tests), and selected-closure Cypress (23 passed, none skipped). The Cypress runner left three generated PNGs in unignored `apps/web/cypress/screenshots/`. The next enabled pre-push hook included them as source changes, invalidated the successful validation receipt, and failed with `Browser evidence is not admitted ... declare every affected spec and its real runtime`.

All generated captures were preserved under `.dvt/evidence/3557-cypress/`; the source worktree is clean. No hook was bypassed, no validation receipt fabricated, and no failed check called green. Publication/integration of the product fix remains pending.

## Proposed bounded cut

- Give generated Cypress captures one explicit evidence owner and output location outside the source inventory. Keep real authored fixtures governed; do not blanket-ignore browser inputs.
- Preserve the last successful exact-input validation receipt when a different input fails. It must never satisfy the changed input, but should remain reusable when the exact previously validated state is restored. No force-success path, mutable-input trust, or check reduction.
- Align the runner, artifact collection, Git inventory, and receipt lifecycle. No new workflow family or redesign of CI.

## Current and intended state

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Validated source commit] --> B[Cypress emits unignored captures]
  B --> C[Hook counts captures as source inputs]
  C --> D[Deletes valid receipt and rejects evidence]
  D --> E[Unnecessary full rerun after captures are moved]
```

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  A[Source inputs] --> B[Exact-input validation]
  B --> C[Bounded successful receipt]
  B --> D[Captures owned by ignored evidence output]
  E[Changed input fails] --> F[Cannot reuse old receipt for changed input]
  F --> G[Restored identical input can reuse its actual successful receipt]
```

## Acceptance

- The existing live proof still runs all 23 Cypress cases and retains captures.
- A green gate does not dirty the source inventory or make its own next push fail.
- Negative tests reject source/head/base/staged/untracked/validation-level drift.
- A failed different-state run does not erase actual evidence for the previously validated state.
- Hooks remain enabled; no fake stamps, skipped checks, timeout increases, or coverage reductions.
- Governing sources: AGENTS.md, governance inventory, pr-preflight-and-ci-triage, the existing prepush stamp and browser-evidence routing rules. Consult authoritative Planning DB CI designs and record the admitted scope before implementation.

Separate existing execution concern: default local parallel presentation pool timed out 20/926 tests in 312.99 seconds; the unchanged one-worker CI profile passed all 926 in 1198.06 seconds. This is not a speedup. Keep concurrency/preparation optimization separate from the artifact/receipt cut.
title: ci(ci): Keep generated browser evidence out of source validation inputs

### Description

When a Phrase Maker has graphics rows (`forward`, `back`, `right`, `left`, `set color`, ...) and you press Play in the widget after loading a project, the turtle on the canvas doesn't move. The graphics are done by a hidden, trashed turtle instead.

`PhraseMakerAudio._processGraphics` (`js/widgets/PhraseMakerAudio.js`) always draws with turtle 0:

```js
_processGraphics(pm, obj) {
    const firstTurtle = pm.activity.turtles.getTurtle(0);
    switch (obj[0]) {
        case "forward":
            firstTurtle.painter.doForward(obj[1]);
    ...
```

Loading a project trashes the turtles of the previous project but leaves them in the turtle list, so turtle 0 is the trashed (hidden) turtle of the old project, and the loaded project runs on another turtle. The Phrase Maker then moves turtle 0, which you can't see, and the project's turtle stays where it is. The same goes for a Phrase Maker under any start block other than the first, which should move its own turtle rather than the first one (that case I didn't test).

### Expected Behavior

Playing graphics rows in the Phrase Maker should move and draw with the turtle that ran the Phrase Maker block, i.e. the turtle you see on the canvas.

### Screenshots

N/A (the turtle just doesn't move)

### How to Reproduce

1. Load a project with a start block and a Phrase Maker containing a `forward 100` row, for example `cypress/fixtures/phrase-maker-minimal.tb` from the repo (it has `forward 100` and `right 90` rows).
2. Press Play. The Phrase Maker opens.
3. Mark the first cell of the `forward` row and press Play in the Phrase Maker.
4. The turtle on the canvas doesn't move.

I checked this on current master with a Cypress run of those steps against the real app, reading the turtles' positions before and after Play:

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| turtle 0 (trashed, from the project before the load) | y = 0 | y = 100 |
| turtle 1 (the loaded project's turtle) | y = 0 | y = 0 |

### Console log Errors:

None.

### Environment:

-   Operating System: Windows 11
-   Browser (if applicable): Chrome
-   Version of Software/Project: current master

### Checklist

-   [x] I have read and followed the project's code of conduct.
-   [x] I have searched for similar issues before creating this one.
-   [x] I have provided all the necessary information to understand and reproduce the issue.
-   [x] I am willing to contribute to the resolution of this issue.

Related: this is the same turtle 0 assumption as #9321 (Meter widget tempo). Many widgets also read `ithTurtle(0).singer.keySignature` (Phrase Maker, Pitch-Drum Matrix, Arpeggio, Music Keyboard, ...), which after a load is the trashed turtle's key; I haven't tested those, so this issue is only about the Phrase Maker graphics.

Update the frontend to consume the restructured `WorkspaceKind.spec.podTemplate` shape introduced on the backend. Bump `workspaces/frontend/scripts/swagger.version` to the backend commit SHA that lands the new schema, regenerate the OpenAPI client (`npm run generate:api`), then follow TypeScript compile errors through the codebase until the feature parity is restored.

**Key files to update:**

| File | Role |
|---|---|
| `workspaces/frontend/scripts/swagger.version` | Pin to the backend commit that introduces the new schema |
| `workspaces/frontend/src/generated/data-contracts.ts` | Regenerated — must not be hand-edited |

| `workspaces/frontend/src/shared/mock/mockBuilder.ts` | Shared mock builder used across tests and Cypress |

**Expected behavior:**

The WorkspaceKind form renders, edits, and submits exactly the same set of fields it does today — pod `securityContext`, pod `schedulerName`, pod `extraVolumes`, container `securityContext`, startup/liveness/readiness probes, container `extraEnv`, container `extraVolumeMounts`, and the `home` mount path — but each field is now bound to its new path in the API payload. Submitting an edited WorkspaceKind round-trips through the backend without data loss. Mocks and Cypress fixtures reflect the new shape so component and E2E tests exercise the real payload layout.

The frontend must not re-introduce any references to the old field names, even in commented-out code or dead branches. - [ ] Workspace create/edit flows that resolve defaults from a parent `WorkspaceKind` continue to pick up the same effective values they did before the restructure.
- [ ] Shared mocks (`mockBuilder.ts`) and test fixtures use the new shape, and existing component and Cypress specs covering WorkspaceKind forms exercise it.
- [ ] A grep of `workspaces/frontend/src/` for the old field paths listed above returns no hits.

## Why

The name "Structured Data Mapper" covers only the schema.org part of the module. SEO tools use "structured data" for schema.org JSON-LD, and the module also writes Open Graph tags. "Mapper" names how the settings screen works, not what the module writes.

The new name `opengraph-schemaorg-metadata` names the two standards that the module writes:

- The mapping form has one switch for Open Graph and one switch for schema.org.
- The Content Editor shows one fieldset for Open Graph and one fieldset for schema.org.
- Drupal uses the same two words: the Metatag module has a submodule for Open Graph, and a second module is called Schema.org Metatag.

The module has no release and no tag, so a rename now changes no installed site.

## New names

| Item                               | Old name                                                     | New name                                                     |
| ---------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Repository                         | `Jahia/structured-data-mapper`                               | `Jahia/opengraph-schemaorg-metadata`                         |
| Maven artifactId and module id     | `structured-data-mapper`                                     | `opengraph-schemaorg-metadata`                               |
| Display name                       | `Structured Data Mapper`                                     | `Open Graph & Schema.org Metadata`                           |
| jContent entry and screen title    | `Structured data`                                            | `Open Graph & schema.org`                                    |
| Java package                       | `org.jahia.pm.modules.structureddatamapper`                  | `org.jahia.pm.modules.opengraphschemaorgmetadata`            |
| Java class prefix                  | `StructuredDataMapper`                                       | `OpenGraphSchemaOrgMetadata`                                 |
| npm package                        | `structureddatamapper`                                       | `opengraphschemaorgmetadata`                                 |
| Permission                         | `structuredDataMapperManage`                                 | `openGraphSchemaOrgMetadataManage`                           |
| i18n namespace and resource bundle | `structured-data-mapper`                                     | `opengraph-schemaorg-metadata`                               |
| CND prefixes                       | `sdm`, `sdmnt`, `sdmmix`                                     | `osm`, `osmnt`, `osmmix`                                     |
| CND namespace URIs                 | `http://www.jahia.org/structured-data-mapper/…`              | `http://www.jahia.org/opengraph-schemaorg-metadata/…`        |
| Selector types and components      | `SdmPreview`, `SdmSchemaPreview`, `SdmTag`, `SdmSchemaValue` | `OsmPreview`, `OsmSchemaPreview`, `OsmTag`, `OsmSchemaValue` |
| Cypress site key                   | `sdmSite`                                                    | `osmSite`                                                    |

The short form `osm` appears only in the CND prefixes, in the selector types and in the Cypress site key. Every other name uses the full name.

The jContent entry in the SEO group and the title of its screen are `Structured data` since [Jahia/structured-data-mapper#48](https://github.com/Jahia/structured-data-mapper/pull/48). The new label is the same in English, German and French, because Open Graph and schema.org are proper names.

The npm package name keeps no hyphen. `CLAUDE.md` states that a hyphen in this name blocks the rendering of the UI.

## Files to change

- Build and repository:
  - `pom.xml`: the artifactId, the name and the three `scm` URLs.
  - `package.json`: the name.
  - `README.md` and `CLAUDE.md`.
- CI:
  - `.github/workflows/on-code-change.yml` and `.github/workflows/on-merge.yml`: `module_id` and `artifact_prefix`.
  - `.github/workflows/schedule-sonar.yml`: `module_id`, `incident_service` and `github_slug`.
- Changelog:
  - `.chachalog/config.mjs`: the package name.
  - The 25 fragments under `.chachalog/` that name `structured-data-mapper` in their front matter.
- Java:
  - The package directory under `src/main/java/` and under `src/test/java/`.
  - The four classes `StructuredDataMapperExtensionsProvider`, `StructuredDataMapperMutationExtension`, `StructuredDataMapperNodeExtension` and `StructuredDataMapperQueryExtension` in the package `graphql`.
  - The constant `MANAGE_PERMISSION` in `OpenGraphService.java`.
- Definitions and forms:
  - `src/main/resources/META-INF/definitions.cnd`.
  - The five forms files under `src/main/resources/META-INF/jahia-content-editor-forms/forms/`, for their file names and their content.
  - Remove `src/main/resources/META-INF/patches/groovy/01-addSwitchMixins.started.groovy`. This patch adds `sdmmix:openGraph` and `sdmmix:schemaOrg` to the mappings stored before [Jahia/structured-data-mapper#42](https://github.com/Jahia/structured-data-mapper/pull/42). Under the `osm` prefix, no mapping of that age exists.
- Permissions: `src/main/import/permissions.xml` and `src/main/import/roles.xml`.
- Labels:
  - `src/main/resources/resources/structured-data-mapper.properties`, for its file name, its keys and its two labels that say `Structured data`.
  - `src/main/resources/javascript/locales/en.json`, `de.json` and `fr.json`: the display name in `label`, and the new label in `mappings.nav` and `mappings.title`.
- UI:
  - `src/javascript/i18n.ts`: `NAMESPACE`.
  - `src/javascript/init.tsx`: the registration function, the callback key, the admin route key, the label key, the permission, `requireModuleInstalledOnSite` and the four selector types.
  - `src/javascript/editor-tags/SdmTag.tsx`, `src/javascript/editor-tags/SdmSchemaValue.tsx` and `src/javascript/editor-tags/sdmTag.gql.ts`.
- Tests:
  - `tests/package.json`, `tests/.env.example` and `tests/provisioning-manifest-snapshot.yml`.
  - The folder `tests/cypress/fixtures/graphql/structuredDataMapper/` and the file `tests/cypress/support/structuredDataMapper.ts`.
  - The site key `sdmSite` in the specs.

## Changes outside the repository

- GitHub redirects the old URL of the repository after the rename. Each local clone can point its remote to the new URL.
- The shared Sonar workflow receives `module_id`. Check whether the workflow builds the key of the Sonar project from this value. A new key starts a new Sonar project with no history.
- The value of `incident_service` names a service outside this repository. Create `opengraph-schemaorg-metadata-sonar` in that service, or keep the old value.
- A Jahia that runs the old module keeps its mappings as `sdmnt:typeMapping` nodes, and its contents keep the `sdmmix:*` mixins. The renamed module does not read these nodes. On such a Jahia, remove the old module and its nodes, then create the mappings again.

## Out of scope

Several names in the GraphQL API and in the Java code start with `openGraph`, and they now cover schema.org too. Examples are `openGraphMappings`, `saveOpenGraphMapping`, `OpenGraphService` and `OpenGraphFilter`. A rename of these names needs a separate issue.

## How to verify

- `git grep -niE 'structured.?data.?mapper|sdm'` finds only links to earlier issues and pull requests.
- `mvn -s .github/maven.settings.xml clean install` writes `target/opengraph-schemaorg-metadata-0.1.0-SNAPSHOT.jar`.
- On a Jahia, the bundle `opengraph-schemaorg-metadata` is `ACTIVE`.
- The `editor-in-chief` role holds `openGraphSchemaOrgMetadataManage`, and a user with this role sees the screen in the SEO group of a site.
- The Cypress suite passes.

## How the list was built

The list comes from the files of `main` at commit `51f1297`, on 2026-11-03. The search was `grep -rniE 'structured[-_ ]?data[-_ ]?mapper|structureddatamapper|sdm|structured data|structuredData'`, without `node_modules`, `target` and `yarn.lock`. The search can miss a name that is built at run time, so run the `git grep` of the verification after the change.

## Update

This issue was updated twice on 2026-11-03:

- The first version proposed the name `social-schema-metadata`.

## Feature
**Cobertura Cypress de correção, painel e relatórios** rodando contra a API e o banco da N2, e não mais contra o `localStorage`. Telas cobertas:
- P15: enviar folhas
- P16: revisar e confirmar
- P17: pendentes de atribuição
- P1: painel
- P2: meu perfil
- P18: relatório da aplicação
- P19: relatório consolidado

O que existe hoje em `apps/web/cypress/e2e`:
- `grading.cy.ts`: leitura simulada, revisão e um bloco de relatório da aplicação.
- `dashboard.cy.ts`: painel e perfil.
- A P19 não tem spec. A P17 só tem um teste de link.
- `cypress/support/e2e.ts` limpa o `localStorage` antes de cada teste, porque os dados vinham do seed do navegador. Com a API, isso deixa de isolar um teste do outro.

## O que fazer no código
**1. Cada spec cria os próprios dados pela API.**
- Escreva comandos em `cypress/support/commands.ts` usando `cy.request`, por exemplo `cy.loginByApi` e um comando que monta uma aplicação gerada com prova mista. Eles fazem login com um professor de teste e criam turma, alunos, questões, prova e aplicação.
- Nenhum spec depende de dado criado por outro, nem da ordem de execução.
- Para testar o isolamento, crie um segundo professor.

**2. O CI precisa da API.** O job Cypress de `.github/workflows/pr.yml` roda `npm run test:e2e`, que hoje sobe só o `preview` (`start-server-and-test preview http://localhost:4173`). Ele passa a subir também a API e um MySQL de teste, com a URL da API vindo da variável de ambiente da #38. Combine com a #39, que roda as migrations e os testes da API no CI.

**3. Specs por tela.** Cada uma cobre fluxo feliz, erro e estado vazio:
- **`grading.cy.ts` (P15, P16, P17):**
  - P15: enviar uma foto real de folha impressa, guardada em `cypress/fixtures/`, com `selectFile` pelo rótulo "Fotografar folha"; arquivo que não é imagem é recusado; aplicação sem folhas mostra o estado vazio.
  - P16: "Salvar sem finalizar" deixa a folha em andamento; "Confirmar correção" com a discursiva valendo 0 conclui a correção.
  - P17: atribuir um aluno; conflito de aluno repetido; "Nenhuma pendência".
- **`dashboard.cy.ts` (P1, P2):**
  - os números do painel batem com o que foi criado pela API;
  - "Corrigir folhas" (#77) com uma, várias e nenhuma aplicação gerada;
  - o perfil mostra o nome real;
  - anonimizar, sempre com uma conta descartável criada no próprio teste.
- **Novo `reports.cy.ts` (P18, P19):**
  - lance notas conhecidas pela API (por exemplo 4, 6 e 8) e confira média 6 e mediana 6 na tela;
  - correção em andamento fica fora da média;
  - a P19 mostra a linha da aplicação, e sem correção mostra "Nenhuma aplicação corrigida".
- **Erro:** `cy.intercept` respondendo 500 numa rota mostra a mensagem de erro da tela (`QueryBoundary`), sem quebrar a página.
- **Isolamento:** o segundo professor abre a URL da aplicação, da revisão ou do relatório do primeiro e vê "não encontrado".
- Opcional: acrescente `/relatorios`, `/perfil` e a P15 à lista `SCREENS` de `responsive.cy.ts`, porque a P15 é usada no celular.

**4. Regras de Cypress do `CLAUDE.md`.** O `grading.cy.ts` atual já quebra algumas delas. Corrija ao mexer:
- Seletor preso à tag: `input[aria-label="Marcar a folha 1 para leitura"]`, `img[alt*="Folha de respostas"]` e `button[aria-label="Girar a folha"]`. Use o nome acessível, com `cy.findByLabel` e `cy.contains`.
- Índice em vez de nome: `input[aria-label^="Nota da questão"]` com `.first()`. Escolha pela questão.
- Montar URL a partir de `cy.url()` com `url.split('/')[4]`: prefira navegar pelos links do próprio app.
- Espere o que a tela mostra quando está pronta antes de agir.
- Não use `cy.visit` nem `cy.reload` com uma gravação ainda em andamento.
- `.as()` não congela valor: para comparar antes e depois, guarde o valor numa variável dentro de `.then()`.

## Fora desta tarefa
- Specs de banco de questões e provas: #63. De turmas e aplicações: #59. De acesso e consulta pública: #55
- Os bugs encontrados no teste exploratório: issues próprias, abertas na #66

### Checklist de aceite
- [x] Specs de correção, revisão, pendentes, painel, relatórios e perfil cobrindo fluxo feliz, erro e estado vazio, contra a API e o banco
- [x] Cada spec cria os próprios dados pela API e não depende da ordem de execução
- [x] Seletores por nome acessível, nunca por tag ou índice, inclusive nos testes que já existem em `grading.cy.ts`
- [x] Um professor não abre a aplicação, a correção nem o relatório de outro
- [x] Suíte inteira verde no CI, com a API e o banco de teste no job do Cypress
- [x] Testes automatizados do caso principal
- [ ] Vídeo do teste anexado no PR

### Prazo
2026-10-22

### Depende de
#66 (teste exploratório de correção, painel e relatórios), #47, #48, #50 e #77 (as telas integradas), #39 (API e banco no CI)

### Referências
- `CLAUDE.md`: "O Cypress roda local" e "O Cypress cobre o sistema inteiro"
- `docs/CI_CD.md`: passo 6 e "O Cypress precisa da aplicação servida"
- `apps/web/cypress/e2e/grading.cy.ts`, `dashboard.cy.ts` e `responsive.cy.ts`
- `apps/web/cypress/support/commands.ts` (`findByLabel`, `findInDialog`) e `e2e.ts`
- `.github/workflows/pr.yml`: o job Cypress

## User story

As an OIOIOI maintainer, I want the Cypress test project (`oioioi_cypress`) to use current, maintained packages. Then the nightly E2E suite runs on a modern, supported toolchain, and the npm Dependabot alerts caused only by these old test dependencies go away.

Right now **31 of the 49 open npm Dependabot alerts** come only from the `oioioi_cypress` importer in `pnpm-lock.yaml`:

| Vulnerable package | Path in `pnpm-lock.yaml` | Dependabot alerts | Fixed by |
|---|---|---|---|
| `axios@0.25.0` | `wait-on@6.0.1` → `axios` | 23 (239–253, 258–260, 265–267, 316, 317; up to high) | `wait-on@9` (uses `axios@^1.20`) |
| `extract-zip@2.0.1` | `cypress@13` → `extract-zip` | 2 (367, 389; high, **no patched version**) | `cypress@16` (no longer depends on it) |
| `tmp@0.2.5` | `cypress@13` → `tmp` | 1 (256; high) | `cypress@16` → `tmp@~0.2.4` → 0.2.7 |
| `form-data@4.0.5` | `cypress` → `@cypress/request@3` → `form-data` | 1 (272; high) | `@cypress/request@4` → `form-data` 4.0.6 |
| `qs@6.14.2` | `cypress` → `@cypress/request@3` → `qs` | 3 (255, 379, 383) | `@cypress/request@4` (`qs@^6.15.2`) → 6.16.0 |
| `uuid@8.3.2` | `cypress` → `@cypress/request@3` → `uuid` | 1 (254) | `@cypress/request@4` (no longer depends on it) |

Alert numbers refer to https://github.com/sio2project/oioioi/security/dependabot (as of 2026-10-18).

## Current state (`oioioi_cypress/package.json`)

| Package | Specifier | Locked | Latest | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cypress` | `^13.7.2` | 13.17.0 | 16.2.0 | 16 needs Node `^22 \|\| ^24 \|\| >=26`. CI and Docker are on Node 24 (#828) |
| `wait-on` | `^6.0.1` | 6.0.1 | 9.5.1 | Node ≥20. Used only as a CLI in `test_cypress.sh` |
| `cypress-file-upload` | `^5.0.8` | 5.0.8 | 5.0.8 (2021) | Unmaintained. Cypress has had native `.selectFile()` since 9.3 |
| `@types/uuid` | `^8.3.4` | 8.3.4 | 11.0.0 (deprecated stub) | `uuid` ships its own types |
| `uuid` | `^14.0.0` | 14.0.0 | 14.0.3 | already current |
| `typescript` | `^5.4.4` | 5.9.3 | 7.0.2 | see Out of scope |
| `@types/node` | `^24.0.0` | 24.x | 26.x | matches Node 24 in Docker/CI, so keep it |

## Proposed tasks

### Must
- [x] Bump `cypress` to `^16`. Check `cypress.config.ts` against the v14/v15/v16 migration guides (see Notes; we don't seem to use any of the breaking APIs). (#837)
- [x] Bump `wait-on` to `^9`. Check that the flags in `test_cypress.sh` (`--simultaneous 1 --interval 1000 --httpTimeout 10000 --timeout 120000`, see #826) still work. (#837)
- [x] Replace `cypress-file-upload` with native `.selectFile()`: (#837)
  - `cypress/e2e/user/submit.cy.ts`: 2× `.attachFile(file, { subjectType: "drag-n-drop" })` → `.selectFile("cypress/fixtures/" + file, { action: "drag-drop" })` (`selectFile` paths are relative to the project root, not `fixtures/`)
  - remove `import "cypress-file-upload"` from `submit.cy.ts` and `contest/settings.cy.ts`
  - remove `"cypress-file-upload"` from `tsconfig.json` `types` and from `package.json`
- [x] Remove the `@types/uuid` dependency (deprecated stub). (#837)
- [x] Regenerate `pnpm-lock.yaml` (`pnpm install`, pnpm 12, keeping the 7-day `minimumReleaseAge`). Check that `axios@0.x`, `extract-zip`, `@cypress/request@3` and `uuid@8` are gone from the lockfile. (#837)
- [x] Run the Cypress workflow (`workflow_dispatch` on `cypress.yml`) and make sure all 3 specs pass. (#837)

### Nice to have
- [x] Clean up leftovers: drop the empty `cypress/plugins/index.ts` and its `setupNodeEvents` require in `cypress.config.ts`, the CRA-style `browserslist` block in `package.json`, and the unused `multi-reporter-config.json` (it points at `cypress-parallel`, which is not installed). (#837)
- [x] Fix the Windows-only `set NODE_ENV=development&` prefixes in the `cy:*` scripts (on Linux/macOS they don't set anything). (#837)
- [x] Bump `tsconfig.json` `target`/`lib` from `es2021` to `es2022`. (#837)
- [x] Add the `npm` ecosystem to `.github/dependabot.yml` (directory `/`, which covers the pnpm workspace including `oioioi_cypress`), weekly, with grouped minor and patch updates and the same 7-day `cooldown` as the `github-actions` entry. (#837)

## Out of scope
- TypeScript 7 (native Go compiler, no JS compiler API). Cypress's TS preprocessing still relies on the `typescript` package, so stay on 5.x (optionally try 6.x, the last JS-based release).
- Rewriting the specs, adding new tests, or moving to component testing / `cy.session`.
- Root-workspace npm alerts (`fast-uri`, `browserslist`, `baseline-browser-mapping`, `shell-quote`, `@humanfs/node`). They come from webpack, concurrently and eslint, not from `oioioi_cypress`, so they need a separate issue.

## Notes
- Cypress 15 breaking changes: removed Node 18/23 support, changed `cy.exec()` result `code` → `exitCode`, dropped CDP for Firefox. Cypress 16: `cy.intercept` uses native browser network interception, and `getCookie` overrides need `Cypress.Commands.overwriteQuery`. Our specs use none of these (`browser: 'electron'`, no `cy.intercept` / `cy.exec`).
- Cypress 15.21+ also drops `extract-zip` and uses `@cypress/request@4`. It is the fallback if 16 causes problems.

## Related
- #828 (CI / Node 24 modernization)
- #826 (wait-on flooding the dev server)

## Summary

A heading's chat channel id is the heading's `toc-id`, and `channels.id` is one global primary key. The webapp opens a channel by that id alone, with no `workspace_id` check. So another document's channel row can answer for this document's heading. A signed-in user can insert such a row, and every duplicate already shares its source's rows.

- **Severity:** Medium. Impact:
  - **Foreign row.** A user creates a channel row whose id is another document's heading `toc-id`, under their own document. It works only for a heading whose chat nobody has opened yet. That heading's chat then opens the foreign row. Messages posted there belong to the creator's document, and the creator is the row's ADMIN member.
  - **Duplicate.** `duplicateDocument` copies the Yjs bytes, so the copy keeps every `toc-id`. Heading chat in the copy opens the source's channels. A public copy of a Private document shows the source's chat. Only the owner can duplicate, so this leak needs an owner action.
  - **After #396.** Once Private chat is gated, a foreign row in a public document would bypass that gate.
- **Area:** Supabase `channels`, webapp chatroom, MCP chat store
- **Source:** security review of 2026-10-06, finding M4

## Production check (2026-10-06, read-only)

- Policy `channels_member_insert`: `WITH CHECK (created_by = auth.uid() AND internal.is_workspace_member(workspace_id))`. Any id is accepted.
- `authenticated` holds INSERT on every `channels` column, including `id`, `type`, `workspace_id` and `member_count`.
- `workspaces` keys: `PRIMARY KEY (id)`, `UNIQUE (slug)`. Channels have a global `PRIMARY KEY (id)`.
- Migration `20261006130000_close_client_write_and_grant_gaps.sql` (#401) later revoked UPDATE on `channels`. INSERT is unchanged.

## Where

- `syncChannel` reads by id alone and reuses any row: `apps/webapp/src/components/chatroom/hooks/useChannelMetadata.ts:24-71`.
- `upsertChannel` uses `onConflict: 'id', ignoreDuplicates: true`, so a taken id silently writes nothing: `apps/webapp/src/api/channels/newChannel.ts:6-12`.
- `get_channel_aggregate_data` looks up `c.id` only: `packages/supabase/scripts/10-functions.sql:84-85`.
- Insert grant and policy: `packages/supabase/scripts/13-RLS.sql:32` and `:125-130`.
- `channels.slug` is globally unique (`packages/supabase/scripts/04-channels.sql:9`). The webapp sets it to `'c' + slugify(channelId)` (`useChannelMetadata.ts:45-51`).
- `add_channel_creator_as_admin` makes the creator an ADMIN member: `packages/supabase/scripts/10-2-func-channels.sql:16`.
- Channel id = heading `toc-id`: `apps/webapp/src/services/openHeadingChatroom.ts:77`. The chat store keeps one `chatRoom.headingId` and uses it as the channel id (`apps/webapp/src/stores/chat/chatroom.ts:12,49-51`).
- Duplicate copies Yjs bytes: `duplicateDocument` in `apps/hocuspocus.server/src/api/services/documents.service.ts:813-929`.
- The MCP chat store already filters on `workspace_id`, but it still treats a heading id as `channels.id`: `apps/hocuspocus.server/src/modules/mcp/infra/chatStore.ts:32-113` and `apps/hocuspocus.server/CLAUDE.md:140`.

## Root cause

The channel key is a client-chosen global id, not a per-document key. The first insert of an id owns it.

## Fix plan

Key heading channels by `(workspace_id, heading_id)`. Existing rows keep their `id`, so messages, media paths (`{userId}/{channelId}/…`), realtime topics and old links do not change.

1. **Schema (migration + `scripts/04-channels.sql`).**
   - Add `heading_id varchar(36)` to `public.channels`. Backfill `heading_id = id` for every row, then set it `not null`.
   - Add `unique (workspace_id, heading_id)`.
   - Replace the global `unique (slug)` with `unique (workspace_id, slug)`. A client still chooses `slug`, so a global key would let a user take another document's slug and block its channel. The client keeps sending `'c' + slugify(headingId)`.
   - Two server-side writers insert channels. Set `heading_id` in both, and recreate both in the migration:
     - `notify_user_join_workspace` (`scripts/10-8-func-workspace_members.sql:28-45`): `heading_id = new.workspace_id`.
     - The DIRECT channel insert in `scripts/10-functions.sql:511`: `heading_id = new_channel_id`.
2. **Insert grant (migration + `scripts/13-RLS.sql:32`).** Replace the table-wide INSERT with `INSERT (workspace_id, heading_id, created_by, name, slug)`. A client can no longer choose `id`, `type`, `member_count` or `deleted_at`. New rows take the default `id`.
3. **Webapp: one resolve point.** The chat store keeps `headingId` for UI and TOC, and adds the resolved `channelId` for database reads, writes and realtime topics.
   - `syncChannel` finds the row by `(workspaceId, headingId)`. If none exists, it upserts with `onConflict: 'workspace_id,heading_id'`, then reads again.
   - List the uses of `chatRoom.headingId` with `grep -rnE "chatRoom\??\.headingId" apps/webapp/src` (27 hits today). Switch each one that reads or writes the database to `chatRoom.channelId`.
   - TOC unread badges map rows by `heading_id`: `apps/webapp/src/services/headingWidgetUnread.ts:33-41` and `apps/webapp/src/api/channels/getChannels.ts`.
   - The chatroom Cypress fixtures own all Supabase HTTP. Update any fixture that stubs the channel read by `id`.
4. **Webapp: links.** Push, email, digest, report and copy-link URLs carry a channel id. Keep those builders as they are. The link entry points read the row by `id`, refuse a row whose `workspace_id` is not the open document, and open its `heading_id`:
   - `apps/webapp/src/hooks/useCheckUrlAndOpenHeadingChat.ts:14-24`
   - `apps/webapp/src/hooks/useNotificationClickBridge.ts:46-52`
   - `openChatAtMessage` in `apps/webapp/src/components/PanelFeedItem.tsx:145-150`
5. **MCP chat store.** `hasRoom`, `readThread` and `postMessage` receive a heading id as `roomId`. Resolve it by `(workspace_id, heading_id)` to the channel `id` before the message query.
6. Run `bun run --filter @docs.plus/supabase_back seed`, then `bun run --filter @docs.plus/supabase_back types`. The new column changes the generated types, so commit `apps/webapp/src/types/supabase.ts`.

Rejected: keep client ids and only check `workspace_id` on read. The foreign row then blocks the real document from creating its channel. Every heading chat in an old duplicate would also stop working.

## Out of scope

- Re-minting `toc-id`s in `duplicateDocument`. The per-document key already keeps a copy's chat separate.
- Changing `get_channel_aggregate_data`. The client passes it the resolved channel id.
- A format check on `channels.id`. Step 2 takes the choice of `id` away from clients, and #436 escapes the id in the selector.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A channel row that document B created with a heading id from document A is never opened by document A's heading chat.
- [ ] A client insert that names `id` is refused with `42501`.
- [ ] Heading chat in a duplicate, old or new, starts empty and does not show the source's messages.
- [ ] Existing heading chats keep their history, unread badges and media.
- [ ] Old links (`?chatroom=`, `c_id`, push, email, digest) still open the right heading chat.
- [ ] A link to a channel of another document does not open it.
- [ ] MCP `list_chat_rooms`, `read_chat_thread` and `post_chat_message` still work on new and old rooms.

## Verify

1. Apply locally: `docker exec -i supabase_db_docsplus_supabase psql -U postgres -d postgres < packages/supabase/migrations/<new file>.sql`.
2. In `psql`, as user B (`set local role authenticated;` plus `request.jwt.claims`), insert a channel under B's document with a heading id from document A. Then open that heading's chat in document A in the local webapp. Expect a new, empty row under document A.
3. In the local webapp, duplicate a document whose headings have chat. Open each heading chat in the copy.
4. Open an old push link, an email link and a copied message link.
5. Run `cd apps/webapp && bun run test`, and the chatroom Cypress suite with `bash scripts/test-chatroom.sh`.

## Related

- #396 Private document chat. Do this issue with it or right after it (see the order of work in #416).
- #436 page crash from a channel row. It escapes the channel id in the heading selector. Neither issue adds a format check on `channels.id`.
- #401 revoked client UPDATE on `channels`.
