### Context / Problem to solve / Design The HTML filtering module checks a rich text property when an editor saves it. Content that existed before the module was installed, or before a rule changed, is not checked again. An administrator therefore cannot know how much content of a site breaks the current rules, before they change the rules or the strategy. This story adds a report that scans the content of a site. The report lists each rich text property whose value does not pass the HTML filtering rules of the site. The report runs in the background on the processing node, and it stops at a configurable maximum number of items. The main feasibility risk is performance. A scan of a large site must not degrade the platform for editors and visitors. The tech notes give the constraints that address this risk. ### Story As a site administrator or a server administrator, I want to see the content of a site that does not pass the HTML filtering rules, So that I can correct that content, or adapt the rules, before I change the filtering of the site. ### Scope #### The properties that the report checks The report must check the same properties as the HTML filtering at save time, with the same result: - The property is of type `STRING` and has the `richtext` selector in the CND. A JSON override does not count, as for the save-time filtering. - The property matches `process` and does not match `skip` in the policy of the site. - The report ignores `skipOnPermissions`. This setting depends on the user who saves the content, and a background scan has no such user. - A value is not valid when `Policy.sanitize` rejects at least one tag or one attribute, which is the condition that `PolicySanitizedHtmlResult.isValid()` returns. The REJECT strategy uses the same condition. - The report checks each value of a multiple property. - The report checks each language of the site. - The strategy of the policy (`REJECT`, `SANITIZE`, or `DISABLED` from [Jahia/html-filtering#190](https://github.com/Jahia/html-filtering/issues/190)) does not change the result. #### The workspace of a run The user chooses the workspace when they run the report: - **Edit**: the report scans the default workspace with the `editWorkspace` policy of the site. This is the default choice. - **Live**: the report scans the live workspace with the `liveWorkspace` policy of the site. #### The content of a row One row is one property of one content node in one language, when its value is not valid. An item in the limits below is one row. A property that is not valid in two languages gives two rows. | Column | Content | | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Path | The path of the content node. | | Property | The name of the property that is not valid. | | Language | The language of the value. The cell is empty for a property that is not internationalized. | | Markups | The markup that the policy rejected: each rejected tag (` | | C | rich text | en | | | D | string, no richtext selector | en | | | E | rich text, internationalized | en |

valid

Same set as `_readme_media` in .github/filters/extensions.yaml. if [[ "${f}" =~ ^extensions/[^/]+/(assets/|[^/]+\.(gif|png|jpe?g|webp|mp4)$) ]]; then echo "media ${f}" >&2; continue fi case "${f}" in package.json|bun.lock|bunfig.toml|tsconfig*.json|tsup.base.ts|.github/*|scripts/*|packages/eslint-config/*|.prettierrc*|.prettierignore|eslint.config.*|.stylelintrc*|docker-compose*.yml) webapp=true; admin=true; backend=true; echo "shared ${f}" >&2; continue ;; esac hit=false case "${f}" in apps/webapp/*|extensions/*|packages/floating-*|packages/supabase/*|packages/pad-url/*) webapp=true; hit=true ;; esac case "${f}" in apps/admin-dashboard/*) admin=true; hit=true ;; esac case "${f}" in apps/hocuspocus.server/*|packages/email-templates/*|packages/pad-url/*|packages/supabase/*|packages/floating-*|extensions/extension-hyperlink/*|extensions/extension-hypermultimedia/*|extensions/extension-inline-code/*) backend=true; hit=true ;; esac if [ "${hit}" = true ]; then echo "scoped ${f}" >&2 else webapp=true; admin=true; backend=true; echo "unmatched ${f}" >&2 fi done [ "${total}" -gt 0 ] || everything no-files [ "${total}" -eq "${FILE_COUNT}" ] || everything count-mismatch docs_only=false [ "${docs}" -eq "${total}" ] && docs_only=true emit_all "${webapp}" "${admin}" "${backend}" "${docs_only}" "files=${total}" ``` - A `case` pattern anchors at the start of the path, so `package.json` and `tsconfig*.json` match only root files. - In a `case` pattern, `*` also matches `/`. That only widens rows 1, 4 and 5, which makes more suites run. Row 3 uses a regex, because a wider match there would skip suites. - Check: `shellcheck .github/scripts/detect-change-scopes.sh` prints nothing, if `shellcheck` is installed. ### Step 2. The test, and prove it by sabotage AGENTS.md §Test Policy case (c) applies. The failure mode is a parsing bug: a path classed as docs or media silently skips a suite that its change can affect. Create `.github/scripts/detect-change-scopes.test.sh`, in the same shape as `parse-build-trigger.test.sh`: ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash # Self-contained test harness for detect-change-scopes.sh (no bats dependency). set -uo pipefail HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)" SCRIPT="${HERE}/detect-change-scopes.sh" PASS=0; FAIL=0 # run [ALL_SCOPES] [FILE_COUNT, default: the line count] -> sets OUT run() { local count="${3-auto}" [ "${count}" != auto ] || count="$(printf '%s' "$1" | grep -c . || true)" OUT="$(printf '%s\n' "$1" | ALL_SCOPES="${2:-false}" FILE_COUNT="${count}" GITHUB_OUTPUT='' bash "${SCRIPT}" 2>/dev/null)" } # expect
title: Run only the CI suites a pull request or push can affect

Parent: #2919. Coordinates with #3342 and #3298. User-approved product slice (2026-10-05).

## Problem and reproduced evidence
The Transform palette exposes input fields and existing calculated outputs together. Reusing output A in B clones A's protobuf expression. Editing A subsequently leaves B evaluated from A's previous definition. This violates the user's dependency expectation. In-memory production commands demonstrated A=TRIM(first_name), B=UPPER(A), C=IS_NOT_NULL(A); replacing A with LOWER(first_name) changes neither B nor C. This is distinct from the still-unattributed generic save rejection in the user's screenshot.

## Approved intent
A calculated alias reused by another field in the same Transform is a stable dependency, not a copied formula. Updating its definition updates dependent results; renaming preserves references; deletion cannot silently break consumers; cycles and incompatible type changes fail closed with actionable localized diagnostics. Inputs and same-Transform calculated fields must be visibly distinguished.

## Governing sources and rail
AGENTS.md; governance-document-rule-inventory; command-query-rail-governance; fowler-opportunity-planning-governance; ADR-0064; existing ConfigureCanvasDvtNode / ProjectCanvasRelationalTree / SaveWorkspaceGraphDraft / PreviewCanvasTransformRows rails. Reuse the pinned Substrait Plan and identity-only V1 sidecar. No second persisted AST, SQL authority, contract V2, migration or provider-specific dependency semantics.

## Definition of Ready
- [x] Root defect reproduced using actual semantic commands, without modifying user data.
- [x] Product dependency semantics approved by user.
- [x] Related expression epic inspected; no competing open implementation PR found.
- [x] Exact representation, before/after diagrams, constrained surfaces and Fowler matrix reviewed by both agents and admitted through existing Planning DB commands before TDD.
- [x] Isolated branch and exact baseline recorded; #3578 remains untouched.

## Definition of Done
- [x] Multi-level and shared dependencies survive save/reload and definition changes.
- [x] Stable field identities survive rename and output reorder.
- [x] Self-reference, cycles, missing/ambiguous references, stale revision and dependent deletion are rejected atomically with specific i18n diagnostics.
- [x] Incompatible type changes leave the canonical document untouched.
- [x] Palette clearly distinguishes input fields and calculated outputs.
- [x] Preview evaluates the same canonical dependent semantics as persisted authoring.
- [x] Unit, semantic/architecture, presentation and one representative browser flow pass; touched-package lint/typecheck, ARC obligations, prepush and exact-base/head Planning DB validation pass before integration.
- [x] No legacy inferred dependencies, stubs, parallel APIs/stores or bypasses; existing copied expressions remain independent because their dependency intent cannot be inferred safely.

## Scope guard
No DuckDB implementation, general SQL function expansion, #3578 CI repair, or claim that the screenshot's save failure has been reproduced. Further design details and evidence are recorded chronologically here.
title: fix(web): Preserve calculated-field dependencies within Transform
